solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Go to loo, involving pee? Here's potential evidence

indicators.note: involving means the first piece wraps round and takes in the second

parts.note: to have a slash is British slang for urinating
pee is how the letter P is spelt out

explanation.surface: A toilet visit leaves tell-tale traces on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: SLASH is British slang for a trip to relieve oneself; P goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash left behind is a mark that could later serve as proof of what happened.

clue.text: Support change in the food order? I think it'll all end in tears

definitions.text: I think it'll all end in tears

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: change in means the letters of the next words are altered into a new order

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A diner asks for a change to the food order, gloomily predicting disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is not the anagram signal; it is the Order of Merit.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet of doom habitually predicts that things will turn out badly.

clue.text: Promotional material, subsequently upheld, to include final further items

indicators.note: subsequently means another copy of the same piece follows on afterwards

parts.note: an ad is promotional material

indicators.note: to include means the reversed piece wraps round the next word
upheld means held up, so in a down clue the second copy is read upwards

parts.note: an ad again
an end is a final part

explanation.surface: Advertising copy, later endorsed, gains a closing section of extra items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promotional material' is used twice; 'subsequently' brings in the second copy, which 'upheld' turns upwards, and 'to include' wraps it round the final part.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are things added at the end of a book or document, extra items.

clue.text: Deer may head off, in retrospect

parts.note: hinds are female deer

indicators.note: head off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: might is the past form of may

explanation.surface: Deer might set off, as seen looking back.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindsight is the understanding that comes from looking back, the same as retrospect.

clue.text: Name of US rocket — you could make it go

parts.note: it is crossword shorthand for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
a go is a turn, as in taking your turn in a game

explanation.surface: Someone boasts about a famous American launch vehicle they could get started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you could make' is link wording: the next two words build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saturn V launch vehicle carried the Apollo missions to the Moon.

clue.text: Dandy vilenesses, possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might come in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A list of the wicked ways a fop might indulge in.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride, envy, gluttony and the rest are the classic vices of Christian teaching, so vilenesses.

clue.text: Card sharp going round Ohio

indicators.note: going round means the first word encircles the second

parts.note: tart means sharp in taste
O is a postal abbreviation for Ohio

explanation.surface: A card cheat on a tour of an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot cards are a pack used in fortune-telling and some card games.

clue.text: Very lively South American city, in our opinion

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, in Brazil
to us means as it seems to us

explanation.surface: We think Rio is a very lively place.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotous means wild and boisterous, full of noisy high spirits.

clue.text: Trace new voodoo after disturbance in coffin

indicators.note: the three words, once disturbed, are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A horror story: someone finds traces of fresh voodoo inside a disturbed coffin.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden overcoat is a jokey slang phrase for a coffin, the last garment one wears.

clue.text: Novel man to end programme during holiday trip

indicators.note: during means the other pieces sit inside the trip

parts.note: a tour is a holiday trip
he is the pronoun for a man
broadcasters sign off to end a programme

explanation.surface: A presenter wraps up a show while away on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the second Sherlock Holmes novel by Arthur Conan Doyle, published in 1890.

clue.text: Cheers someone like B Pitt or K Reeves?

definitions.meaning: cheers is an informal way of expressing gratitude

definitions.text: someone like B Pitt or K Reeves?
definitions.meaning: Brad Pitt and Keanu Reeves are film actors written with initial and surname

explanation.surface: A toast raised to Hollywood leading men.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as T HANKS: Tom Hanks, abbreviated the way the clue abbreviates Brad Pitt and Keanu Reeves.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying cheers in Britain is a casual expression of gratitude.

clue.text: N? It's seen in 'negative' or North, on reflection

indicators.note: seen in means the first word sits inside the rest
on reflection means the words for negative, or and North are read backwards

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for North
it, with the 's working as is

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about what the letter N stands for in some notation.
explanation.definitionFit: N is the chemical symbol for the gas element that makes up most of the air.

clue.text: Suppress prominent figure not offering a view

indicators.note: not offering means one letter is held back and left out

parts.note: a star is a prominent figure in a field
an angle is a point of view

explanation.surface: Someone famous keeps quiet and declines to give an opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not offering a' removes the first A from STARANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle a protest or a sound is to stifle it, choke it off.

clue.text: Street performance mostly tragic stuff

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: busking is performing in the street for money

explanation.surface: A street act that is largely gloomy material.
explanation.definitionFit: The buskin was the high boot of Greek tragic actors, so it stands for tragic drama itself.

clue.text: Tramp holding on to university books — that's sweet

indicators.note: holding means the tramp's word grips the other pieces inside it

parts.note: bum is slang for a tramp

indicators.note: to means the next piece is attached after the previous ones

parts.note: B is short for book, so BB is books
the on side in cricket is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A vagrant clings to some university textbooks, which is nice of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubblegum is a chewy sweet that can be blown into bubbles.

clue.text: Solvent, with nothing invested in a place to live

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, as money is put into something

parts.note: a flat is an apartment, a place to live
O is the zero shape for nothing

explanation.surface: A person stays out of debt despite having put no money into a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Being afloat financially means staying solvent, not sinking into debt.

clue.text: Finish up sound measure that's completely unusual

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to do something is to finish it, as in done and dusted
dB, the decibel, measures loudness
all means completely, as in all gone

explanation.surface: Wrapping up a sound reading that is entirely out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, oddball means strange or eccentric.

clue.text: Relocation of HQ possibly making you look bad

definitions.meaning: read as ..., removing an organisation from its base or headquarters

explanation.surface: A company moving its head office does its image no favours.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase is to degrade, so debasing behaviour lowers how others see you.

clue.text: Attacked arrangement that's working

parts.note: a set-up is an arrangement
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: An assault made on a scheme that is functioning.
explanation.definitionFit: To be set upon is to be assaulted or ambushed.

clue.text: Rock group caught with something by Shakespeare?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
any Shakespeare drama is an old play

explanation.surface: A band is spotted with a Shakespeare text in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Coldplay is a well-known British rock band.

clue.text: Scoundrel provoked by topless clothing for women

indicators.note: topless in a down clue means the word loses its top, first, letter

parts.note: a blouse is a woman's shirt

explanation.surface: A rogue who is roused by a woman going topless.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a contemptible person, named after the parasite.

clue.text: Be lenient or light

definitions.meaning: to ignite and set off a firework

explanation.definitionFit: One phrase means both pardoning an offender and igniting a firework or banger.

clue.text: No soup remains to be cooked after involving good kitchen utensil

indicators.note: involving means the mixed letters take in one more letter
to be cooked means the words are reworked like ingredients into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: No leftover soup to be cooked, a sorry state for the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A measuring spoon is a kitchen tool for quantities such as a teaspoon.

clue.text: Tool providers declining drink

indicators.note: declining means refusing, so the drink is turned away and dropped

parts.note: suppliers are providers of goods
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Equipment suppliers turn down a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliers are a gripping hand tool with pivoting jaws.

clue.text: Incantation, piece with revolutionary skill

parts.note: a chess or draughts piece is called a man

indicators.note: revolutionary means the word for skill is turned round

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A chant described as a work of radical artistry.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or phrase chanted repeatedly, as in meditation.
